summary: QUALITY GATE STILL FAILED: compilation and original paired PDS are insufficient to finish this development task. The checker passes the original 28 core cases and 5/6 boundary cases, but only 13/20 additional confirmation cases. The 20 confirmation labels were independently checked with AddressSanitizer; all match actual bounded-loop executions. Two UNSAFE constructs are suppressed: access in the ELSE arm of an in-bounds test, and an in-bounds-looking comparison against a constant greater than the real array extent. Five SAFE constructs still warn: unconditional early continue on out-of-bounds, unconditional early break at the capacity threshold, safe ELSE arm of an out-of-bounds test, OR where BOTH disjuncts prove the same safety bound, and an early continue dominating the access inside a nested lexical block. Existing guard API only receives the loop variable, so it cannot prove a bound against the actual array: refactor it to reason about the accessed declaration/capacity, branch truth and integer index constraints. Safe-direction matching alone is inadequate. Analyze the TRUE or FALSE predicate according to which branch contains this access; logical AND/OR must combine bounds soundly for that polarity. For preceding exit guards, prove the exit targets this loop and occurs unconditionally on the excluded index range; do not treat a guard nested under an unrelated condition as dominating. Retain warnings if the actual array extent or path proof is unavailable, without syntax-only X-1 fallback. Keep strict/non-strict and reversed loop tests correct. Keep original ASTCodeBody mechanism and no file/function/fixture-name allowlists. Implement the necessary generic helpers, including API signature/call-site updates, rather than only adjusting comments or a single comparison. Do not read fixture files. Exact fixture text has not been included: these are semantic requirements from failures. Candidate code edits must all be model-produced. All observed failures remain archived and this entire continuation is post-hoc development, outside the main 39-case results.
